issues.advice: Serve PNG or JPEG instead, and keep AVIF for the web; a client that cannot decode it shows an empty box; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/image-avif/
issues.message: One image is served as AVIF, which Outlook (Windows, Windows Mail), 1&1, Fastmail and 5 other clients do not support.

markup.advice: Remove the handlers and move what they did to a page the message links to; email clients strip them, and those that keep them do not run them
markup.message: The HTML carries 1 event-handler attribute (onclick on <a>), which no email client runs.

rendering.advice: Use inline CSS instead of external stylesheets for better email compatibility
rendering.message: External stylesheet link detected: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;700&display=swap - may cause rendering issues or privacy concerns

rendering.advice: Place the element with nested tables, cell padding and spacer rows instead; where position is dropped the element falls back into the document flow; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/css-position/
rendering.message: The styles use position in one place, which Gmail, Outlook (Windows, Windows Mail, iOS) and Mail.ru do not support.

rendering.advice: Lay the row out as a table with one cell per column; flexbox is dropped rather than approximated, so its children stack into a single column; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/css-display-flex/
rendering.message: The styles use display:flex in 3 places, which Outlook (Windows, Windows Mail), GMX (Desktop Webmail), Orange and 1 other client do not support.

rendering.advice: Lay the grid out as a table, one row per row and one cell per cell; a client that does not know grid keeps the children and loses their positions; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/css-display-grid/
rendering.message: The styles use display:grid in one place, which Outlook (Windows, Windows Mail), GMX (Desktop Webmail), Orange and 1 other client do not support.

rendering.advice: Decide the order in the markup rather than in the styles; where flex-direction is dropped the children appear in the order they are written; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/css-flex-direction/
rendering.message: The styles use flex-direction:column in 2 places, which Gmail, Outlook (Android, Windows, Windows Mail), Yahoo! Mail and 4 other clients do not support.

rendering.advice: Give the rows and cells their sizes as a table instead; where the grid template is dropped, every child sizes and places itself; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/css-grid-template/
rendering.message: The styles use grid-template-* properties in one place, which Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo! Mail and 4 other clients do not support.

rendering.advice: Name a web-safe font first in every font-family and treat the downloaded one as a bonus; a client that ignores @font-face falls back to a font of its own choosing; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/css-at-font-face/
rendering.message: The styles use @font-face in 2 places, which Gmail, Outlook (Android, Outlook.com, Windows Mail, iOS, macOS), Yahoo! Mail and 10 other clients do not support.

rendering.advice: Move the element into the <head>: a client that accepts a stylesheet at all may still refuse one it finds in the body, and there is nothing to gain by putting it there; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/html-style/
rendering.message: A <style> element is written inside the body, which Gmail (Mobile Webmail), GMX (Desktop Webmail), LaPoste.net and 3 other clients do not support.

rendering.advice: Export the drawing as a PNG and reference it with ; most clients strip inline SVG, leaving the space it occupied empty; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/html-svg/
rendering.message: The HTML uses <svg> in one place, which Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo! Mail and 7 other clients do not support.

rendering.advice: Drop user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the viewport so the recipient can enlarge the text
rendering.message: The viewport forbids zooming, which a recipient who needs to enlarge the text cannot override.

issues.advice: Link to a page instead of to a place in the message, or accept that the jump does nothing: where anchors are not followed the reader stays where they were, and one webmail sends them to its own home page; the client-by-client detail is at https://www.caniemail.com/features/html-anchor-links/
issues.message: One link points to an anchor inside the message itself, which Gmail (iOS), Yahoo! Mail (Android, iOS), Samsung Email and 8 other clients do not support.
